title: Runtime Request Gatekeeper: policy engine + admin telemetry & SSO mappings
creator: Ethan Morales
description:
Summary:
Implement a hardened, low-latency policy evaluation engine and compact authorization middleware (the 'Request Gatekeeper') to enforce RBAC v2 across API, runtime, and Console surfaces. This ticket covers the evaluation runtime, the middleware hooks for API and serving runtime hot-paths, audit emission format and plumbing, SSO/SAML group-to-role claim mapping, and admin controls required to operate RBAC at scale.

Goals:
- Provide a unified Authorization Decision Point (ADP) that can evaluate expressive policies and return allow/deny + reasons within tight p95 latency budget for token-authenticated requests.
- Surface authorization decisions and relevant context to the Console and to downstream audit pipelines for compliance and forensics.
- Support SSO/SAML attributes and group claim mapping to RBAC v2 role bindings.
- Add admin UX controls for role management, emergency breakglass, and delegated admin scopes.
- Migrate safely from RBAC v1 to v2 with incremental rollout and compatibility fallbacks.

Scope / Deliverables:
- A lightweight CEL-compatible policy language for product teams with translations to an optimized engine used in the runtime. We'll ship a small set of builtin predicates (resource, action, principal attributes, time, region, model metadata).
- Compact evaluation engine implemented in Rust (or Go) that can be embedded into the serving runtime and as an HTTP microservice for Console/API. Evaluation must support caching of principals -> computed role bindings and short-lived decision caches.
- Authorization middleware for three surfaces: Redwood API gateway (edge), serving runtime request path (token + model request evaluation), and Console (web actions). Middleware provides a single decision call interface and gracefully degrades to legacy checks when a policy is missing.
- Audit logging schema (JSON lines) and event emitter: decision_id, request_id, principal_id, roles_evaluated, effective_permissions, policy_version, decision, reason, timestamp, latency_ms, service_surface. Events will be emitted synchronously to internal Kafka topic for observability and asynchronously forwarded to SIEM or GCS export.
- SSO/SAML integration: claim mapping config in Console to map SAML/SCIM/OIDC group claims -> RBAC role bindings. Provide tests for overlapping groups and priority rules, and a CLI utility to preview mappings for a given SAML assertion.
- Admin controls in Console: role creation UI, binding inspector, history view (who changed what), and breakglass token issuance with TTL and audit tags.
- Migration plan: feature-flagged rollout per-customer with canary on dedicated accounts, opt-in alpha for internal teams, and automatic fallbacks when migration detects missing role bindings.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Policy engine responds to cached queries <1ms p95 and cold queries <4ms on standard instance types in perf harness.
- Middleware integrates with API gateway and serving runtime with end-to-end test coverage.
- Audit events conform to schema and are visible in Console Events view and in the audit Kafka topic.
- SSO mapping UI and preview feature implemented and validated against production SAML assertions from two partner IdPs.
- Admin breakglass token flow audited and requires two-step approval for issuance in production.
- Security review completed and signed off before broad rollout.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Policy language: we selected a CEL-first surface for authorability by product/security teams. For runtime performance and reuse of existing policy assets we will provide a transpiler that converts CEL to a compact AST used by the Rust engine. Full Rego support was considered but increases bundle size and runtime complexity; we will provide an import tool for Rego -> CEL where feasible.
- Caching: principal-to-binding cache and decision result cache keyed by (principal_hash, resource_hash, action, policy_version). TTL is short (30s) to keep semantics near-real-time for role updates. Long-term caching risks stale allow/deny behavior which is unacceptable for admin revokes.
- Failure modes: middleware will fail-closed by default for admin and sensitive routes; for best-effort user-facing endpoints we will support fail-open as a configurable policy with explicit audit markers.
- Performance isolation: the engine runs as a library in serving runtime for hot-path checks; for Console/API we use sidecar microservice with connection pooling to avoid long GC pauses affecting Console latency.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for policy language, edge cases, and arithmetic/time predicates.
- Integration tests that simulate SSO assertions and group mapping conflicts.
- Load tests against the serving runtime to validate p95 budgets under realistic token churn and batching patterns.
- End-to-end canary on 10 internal teams followed by progressive ramp to 25% of hosted accounts.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: internal alpha for SRE and Platform (feature-flagged).
- Phase 1: opt-in beta for customers with low traffic; validate audit pipeline and SSO mappings.
- Phase 2: canary per-region with traffic shaping and automatic rollback on error budget breaches.
- Phase 3: global enable with migration tooling for RBAC v1 bindings.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Security/RBAC+v2+Gatekeeper (draft)
- Proto/Schema: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/rbac-v2-schema (preview)
- Perf harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2148 (WIP)
- Admin console mockups: https://figma.com/redwood/rbac-v2-admin (view-only)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we need deterministic provenance for policy_version (git sha + deployed timestamp) in audit events? Recommendation: yes.
- How should delegated admin scoping be expressed (resource-level vs folder-level)? Suggested: allow both with precedence rules.
- Tooling for bulk migration from RBAC v1: should live in a separate migration service or be baked into Console? Proposal: migration CLI + Console preview.

Next steps:
- Complete Rust engine prototype and perf baseline (owner: Lena).
- Wire up decision event producer to audit Kafka topic (owner: Samir Rao).
- Console SSO mapping UI prototype review with PM (owner: Maya Chen).
